title: DANCE
mv: Then David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was wearing a linen ephod.
mvp: “Then David danced before the LORD with all his might; and David was wearing a linen ephod.”2 Samuel 6:14 (NKJV)
assignment: Mention five (5) wrong motives for dancing (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Dance is a performing art consisting of a purposefully selected sequence of body movement. It is an outward expression of the moods of an individual in certain circumstances. Dancing is one of those issues that have been questioned in the past. Some groups have viewed all forms of dance as evil. However, joyful dancing has been clearly documented in the Bible (2 Samuel 6:14). Dance can be used as an act of worship to glorify God or for wrongful purposes. Youths should understand the correct perspective and act wisely.

The instances of dancing in the Bible can be categorised into two: dancing to God or with good intentions, and dancing to idols or with evil intentions. The first appearance of God’s people dancing as an act of worship is found with Miriam, the prophetess, Aaron’s sister (Exodus 15:20). Another instance is found in 2 Samuel 6:14, which has David “...danced before the LORD with all his might.” The implication of this is that Christian youths should dance as an act of worship unto God.

In the second category, the Israelites were found dancing before a golden calf in worship and being out of control, they danced naked (Exodus 32:6, 19-25). In this case, dancing led to very sinful activities. Hence, the fact that you can dance or are gifted in the art of dancing does not mean you should dance to every kind of music or at any occasion/gathering where God’s name is not proclaimed or glorified (Ecclesiastes 3:4). This is because, in the process, you may be dancing before idols or to demon-inspired songs/beats.

Youths should avoid sexually stimulating, indecent and seductive body movements while dancing so as not to create wrong impressions (2 Corinthians 12:19-20; Ephesians 4:17-19). Holding or touching of sensual parts of your body or the body of others, in the name of dancing, should be avoided, as this could stimulate sexual urge and impure thoughts (1Thessalonians 5:22). Dancing to bring attention to yourself or your body would not glorify God (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

As long as dance is decent, God-focused and praiseworthy, it can have a proper place in worship (Psalm 149:3). It is important to understand that dance in the context of worship is not simply self-expression. It should be done in a way that is helpful to the entire congregation (Psalm 150:4). Hence, anything during a worship gathering that distracts from a focus on Christ should be left out (1 Corinthians 10:31).

Also, the content of a song (lyrics) and the personality of the singer (whether he or she is a child of God) should be verified before you dance to such songs/beats. You can dance to celebrate God’s faithfulness (Psalm 30:11); appreciate God’s blessings and deliverance (Exodus 15:20); acknowledge God's presence, in anticipation of the manifestation of His victory in your situation.
The believer’s reason for dancing must be to glorify God (1 Corinthians 10:31).

i: What is the right perspective on dancing?
